propositions: A project-owned code-review criterion must enforce four-pass ownership boundaries: Pass 1 discovers only, Pass 2 verifies only, Pass 3 routes deterministically, Pass 4 coaches non-prescriptively.
The criterion implementation must emit grounded candidate findings with no severity, confidence, or suggested_fix fields, and abstain when phase ownership is unclear.

A balanced twelve-case eval corpus (RP-F1..RP-F6 must fire, RP-N1..RP-N6 must not fire) must achieve recall 1.0, false-accept 0.0, agreement 1.0, stability_min ≥ 2/3, and Cohen kappa ≥ 0.70 across three live runs.

The criterion is routed with exec: '1-TURN', single_turn execution mode, and advisory posture (blocking_enabled: false); all changes are restricted to .rebar/ assets, criterion-specific tests, and docs/llm-framework.md.

Pass-1 assessment leaks (validity/impact grading, drop/block policy, remediation instructions), Pass-2 ownership violations (new findings, decisions, fixes), LLM discretion in Pass 3, and Pass-4 re-adjudication or exact prescription must be detected as boundary violations.

The criterion implementation depends on the landed CLI-admission seam story and uses only generic extension points without core special cases; live calibration must confirm perfect metrics before landing on main.
